### Root targeted check of (92)

Using the disjoint partition into X_k^* from scan092, X_j is the union of X_k^* with k <= j. Under faithfulness, X_i^* is nonempty. If X_i^* is contained in X_j, a point of that stratum lies in one of the disjoint X_k^* with k <= j, so k=i and i <= j. The reverse implication follows from the indexing order, and X_i subset X_j implies X_i^* subset X_j. This checks both equivalences (92) and the ensuing order embedding. It does not justify completing the unfinished marginal union identity: the missing union X_K^* is absent from the ink and is removed from both witness readings. The paragraph after “Si on veut Strat 5” is also left unfinished. See CHECK_EVENTS statement150-094-order-embedding.
150_scan095:
### Root mathematical checks and qualification

For A=X_i^* and S=X_j^*, every open neighborhood of A meets S exactly when A meets closure(S): if the latter intersection is empty, X minus closure(S) is a disjoint neighborhood; the converse follows from the definition of closure. This checks the initial pro-neighborhood equivalences under the manuscript's neighborhood interpretation. Since closure(X_j^*) is contained in X_j, the next implication holds, and density makes it an equivalence. The partition implies that X_i^* meeting X_j forces i <= j; faithfulness gives the converse. Thus the displayed one-sided relation is justified under the stated density and faithfulness assumptions.

For the later comparability display, if neither stratum meets the closure of the other, a metric gives disjoint neighborhoods by the inequalities d(x,A)<d(x,B) and d(x,B)<d(x,A). This proves the forward implication to comparability. The reverse caption literally says “strat fidèle.” Read by itself, faithfulness is insufficient: take discrete X={a,b}, I={0<1}, X_0={a}, X_1={a,b}. The open strata are the nonempty singletons {a},{b}, yet their pro-neighborhoods have empty intersection. Density, still present in the preceding paragraph's context, restores the reverse implication. The notes identify that dependence without inserting a missing word into the caption or asserting that the author intended to drop his earlier density assumption. See CHECK_EVENTS statements150-095-neighborhoods and150-095-faithfulness-alone, refined statement150-095-comparability-dense.
150_scan096:
### Root check of the reduction to flags

The pairwise definition on scan095 gives V_{ij}=V_i intersection V_j. Commutativity and idempotence of intersection justify V_{ij}=V_{ji} and V_{ii}=V_i. Under the metrizability setting used there, an incomparable pair has empty pro-neighborhood intersection; hence any finite tuple containing such a pair has empty total intersection. A tuple of mutually comparable indices can be sorted, and repeated indices removed, without changing the intersection. These observations justify the page's reduction to strictly increasing flags. They do not decide whether the written limit mark is an underline or arrow, or the uncertain verb ending: those remain visual questions. See CHECK_EVENTS statement150-096-flag-reduction.

### Root checks of the displayed set relations and the ordered-band reduction

In(106), intersecting V_J with X_L^* is unchanged by additionally intersecting V_L, because X_L^* lies in every neighborhood represented by V_L. Thus equality is mathematically available where the manuscript's heavy connected relation is read only from its strokes. This observation does not resolve the visual subset/equality doubt.

Conditional on the union description in(101) and the incomparable-pair emptiness established on095 in the metrizability setting, distributivity and the three cases j=l, j<l, l<j give the three unions in(107). For(108), use the actual definition J prec L on090: each element of J is below some element of L and each element of L is above some element of J. If l in L lies below j in J, choose j' in J with j' <= l and l' in L with j <= l'. Convexity of the two bands then gives l in J and j in L. Consequently the reverse-order pair intersections are already absorbed by the union indexed by J cap L. This checks that reduction and also explains why a flag meeting both bands starts in J and ends in L, with its J-members an initial segment and its L-members a final segment. No independent categorical colimit or homotopy proof is asserted here. See CHECK_EVENTS statement150-098-band-reduction.
